Questions.

How is it personal?

Every experience is generated for one person and never reused. We find out what gives you chills, and the voice speaks to that exact moment. Each session adapts to how you responded to the last one, so the fifth session knows things about you that the first one could not.

What is a protocol?

A protocol is a set of five sessions built around one thing that gives you chills. The sessions build on each other and on your responses. The ReWire Store also carries protocols designed by world class experts.

What does a session feel like?

Most people describe a wave: a tightness in the chest, goosebumps down the arms, sometimes tears, then a clear thought about what you care about that stays with you afterwards. Headphones help, since every session is built on music and voice.

What if you don't get chills?

It happens, especially at the beginning. Chills come more easily once ReWire has learned how you respond, so the second and third sessions usually land harder than the first. The reflection works either way.

Is this a treatment for depression?

No. These experiences are wellness tools for reflection and emotional wellbeing. They are not medical devices, they have no FDA clearance, and they work best alongside professional care. Our clinical program for depression and anhedonia is separate, in clinical trials, and available only through a clinician. See ReWire DTx.

When can I use it?

The app launches in January 2027. Create your account now, take the test, and join the beta from your profile. Invites go out by email as spots open.

The vision

We design synthetic emotions

ReWire expands the range of what humans can feel. For ten years our team studied how emotions arise in the brain and the body to build an engine that creates them on demand.

How it works

The engine.

A proprietary stack that predicts who will respond, triggers the response, amplifies it through the body, and engages the neural circuit directly.

01
Predict
Personalization
We know what will move you, before you press play.

A multimodal model trained on thousands of labeled chills responses predicts how each person reacts to a given stimulus, reaching AUC 0.76 on held out data.

Schoeller et al., PNAS Nexus, 2024 ↗
02
Induce
Content
We create the content that gives you chills.

Our classifier finds the exact moments that deliver chills in any audio or video. We optimize existing content to raise the response, and generate new content from scratch.

Current induction rate · 74%
03
Augment
Wearable
Amplify the response through the body.

A suite of closed loop interoceptive wearables raises the magnitude and reliability of the bodily response. Currently under clinical investigation.

Schoeller et al., Neurosci. Biobehav. Rev., 2024 ↗
04
Target
Neural
Engage the reward circuit directly.

Closed loop neuromodulation paired with experiential stimuli, through our own pipeline of devices and protocols that engineer specific neural states.

Modalities · tFUS · tDCS · rTMS · VNS

Team

Ten years of R&D

The founders and advisors who built the science, and who hold the platform to a clinical standard.

Founders02
FS
Félix Schoeller, PhD
Founder and Chief Executive Officer · ReWire Neurotechnologies, Inc.

Félix Schoeller is the founder and CEO of ReWire. Over the past decade he has built and led ventures at the intersection of technology and human emotion, taking ideas from concept to clinic, stage, and market. He created the first system capable of reliably inducing aesthetic chills, invented BeSound, a wearable for PTSD under clinical investigation in the Paris public hospital system, and built Lucy, a voice simulation for training psychedelic therapists featured in Nature. With Linc Gasking he invented Huxley, described by Rolling Stone as the first generative AI artist, whose music video for Duran Duran premiered at the 2021 Billboard Music Awards. His ventures have been backed by Joy Ventures, the European Commission, and the French Ministry of Defense, and his work has been published in top-tier journals. He holds a PhD in cognitive science from EHESS Paris and completed postdoctoral work at MIT Media Lab. Outside of work, he can be found hiking and climbing in the mountains of California and Northern Italy.

NR
Nicco Reggente, PhD
Director of Neuroscience · ReWire Neurotechnologies, Inc.

Nicco is a cognitive neuroscientist whose work spans multivariate neuroimaging, closed loop neurotechnology, and computational prediction of treatment response. He holds a PhD in cognitive neuroscience from UCLA and is the cofounder and research director of the Institute for Advanced Consciousness Studies in Los Angeles, where he directs studies on consciousness, emotion, and the neural basis of peak experience. He was lead author on a PNAS paper using resting state functional connectivity to predict treatment response in obsessive compulsive disorder, work that informs the personalization engine inside the ReWire platform.

Advisors03
DP
Diego A. Pizzagalli, PhD
University of California, Irvine · Noel Drury Institute

Diego Pizzagalli is a global authority on the neurobiology of anhedonia and reward processing and ranks among the most cited researchers in depression. He is the founding director of the Noel Drury, M.D. Institute for Translational Depression Discoveries at UC Irvine and the former director of the Center for Depression, Anxiety and Stress Research at Harvard Medical School, where his research defined the field’s understanding of reward system dysfunction. He created the Probabilistic Reward Task, the standard instrument for quantifying blunted reward learning in clinical populations and a core mechanism the ReWire platform aims to address, and he is a coauthor with the ReWire founders on the peer reviewed publications establishing the mechanism behind the platform.

KW
Kim C. Willment, PhD
Harvard Medical School · Brigham and Women's Hospital

Kim Willment is a board certified neuropsychologist, an assistant professor at Harvard Medical School, and the founder and director of the RENEW Program for resilience through neurological and emotional wellness at Brigham and Women’s Hospital. She has spent two decades pioneering the clinical implementation of non pharmacologic interventions for neurological populations, and her expertise in neuropsychological assessment and rehabilitation guides the translation of ReWire’s embodied digital therapeutics from laboratory protocols into real world clinical workflows. She sees ReWire as a tool for both patients and clinicians that helps people reconnect with more expansive, adaptive ways of experiencing themselves and the world.

AM
Adam McGuire, PhD
University of Texas at Tyler · Clinical Psychology PhD Program

Adam McGuire is an associate professor of psychology, a licensed clinical psychologist, and a leading researcher on veterans’ mental health and trauma related disorders. As a federally funded principal investigator he leads clinical trials on positive emotion induction, specifically moral elevation, to treat trauma and comorbid depression, and his expertise in digital affect exposure and trial design for high acuity psychiatric conditions keeps ReWire’s therapeutics grounded in evidence based practice for complex mental health populations.

Research toolkit · free for academic use

A research kit for aesthetic chills

Researchers increasingly want to induce chills reliably in the laboratory. Over the past ten years, our team has built the scientific instrumentation to do exactly that. We are making these tools freely accessible to researchers worldwide, so that together we may discover something new about consciousness and cognition.

Machine learning and synthesis · platform add-on

Advanced APIs.

These capabilities operate on top of the standard ChillsDB toolkit as an API integration. A small implementation fee covers API access and compute, and sponsored credits are available for academic labs.

Prediction enginewith IACS

Match participants to chills stimuli.

Our machine learning model evaluates participant inputs, including personality, music-reward sensitivity, and state affect, to calculate individual elicitation probabilities. Based on our predictive models published in PNAS Nexus, the API dynamically selects the highest-yield stimulus per subject during an experiment.

Generative pipelineby ReWire

Create unique personalized stimuli.

A separate generative pipeline synthesizes bespoke multimodal speech stimuli on demand. The system targets specific individual reward sensitivities and optimizes the probability of eliciting a psychogenic shiver in real time, independently of pre-existing library clips.

The science

How chills reach depression.

Three deficits in depression, and where chills enter.

01
Positive affect

Depression is also the absence of positive emotion.

Alongside negative feelings, people with depression lose the capacity to feel interest, joy, and connection. This loss of positive affect is often left untreated, despite being one of the strongest predictors of treatment response. ReWire DTx reliably shifts positive affect by repeatedly exposing people to intense, embodied positive emotion: an intervention known as positive affect exposure.

The neurobiology of aesthetic chills · Neuroscience and Biobehavioral Reviews, 2024
02
Anhedonia

When reward stops teaching the brain.

Anhedonia is the loss of pleasure and motivation. The brain’s reward system stops learning from positive experiences: good things happen, but they fail to change behavior. A chill is a powerful reward signal with a measurable physical signature. It engages the dopaminergic circuitry impaired in anhedonia, and in a controlled study of 103 participants with depressive symptoms, a single chills session modulated reward learning on the Probabilistic Reward Task.

Aesthetic chills modulate reward learning in anhedonic depression · Journal of Affective Disorders, 2024, n = 103
03
Maladaptive schemas

The beliefs that keep depression in place.

Depression is reinforced by schemas: deeply held beliefs such as “I am worthless” or “nothing will change” that filter new experiences and repeatedly confirm themselves. A chill creates a brief opening. In the moments after one, people report greater clarity and connection, and beliefs that felt fixed become more available for revision. ReWire DTx pairs this state with content designed to target the belief, and in a controlled study of 96 participants with depression, this reduced maladaptive cognition.

Mitigating maladaptive cognition in depression · BMC Psychiatry, 2024, n = 96

ReWire

Extend the limits of your mind

Find out what gives you chills, and where it takes you.

Félix Schoeller · Founder and CEO · Los Angeles, CA.

Most of what happens in a day fits inside what you already know. Your mind sorts it and moves on. Then something arrives that does not fit. You move to a new city. You become a parent. You lose a close friend. Your mind hits the edge of what it understands, and for a while everything feels open. You see the world differently, and you see yourself differently.

You usually notice this moment through your body first. Your heart races. You get butterflies in your stomach. Your breath catches. Your skin tingles. Something in you knows you have gone past the edge of what you knew, and something new is about to come in.

Nobody plans these moments. They arrive, they change you, and they leave. And yet they are the reason we are here. The same feeling carried our ancestors out of Africa to see what was past the horizon, and along the way it taught us to care for one another.

ReWire exists to bring you there again. We have spent ten years studying what happens at the edge of the mind. Now we are building software, hardware, and neurotechnologies that take you there on purpose. Create your ReWire account today and discover the films and music that gave people chills in the largest study ever done. See what they reveal about you, and how much you share with the people you love.
